problem: VLM-based VLN methods use either imitation learning (with DAgger) or GRPO-style RL on existing in-distribution trajectories; the two are not integrated, so IL stays limited by expert data and RL on fixed trajectories does not address covariate shift at inference.
motivation: IL suffers from covariate shift and heavy reliance on demonstrations, while RL from verifiable rewards improves reasoning and exploration but is applied to existing trajectories. Combining on-policy exploration with off-policy DAgger supervision should give both error recovery and better generalization.
key_idea: A three-stage pipeline (multi-task IL, DAgger IL, then CHORD-style joint GRPO + IL on DAgger trajectories) with high-entropy trajectory sampling for RL and error-correction-prioritized sorting for IL.
insight: DAgger data gives the largest jump (SR 49.9 to 64.4 in Stage 2). Mixing RL and IL (CHORD, SR 68.7) beats pure GRPO (67.5) and pure IL in Stage 3 (68.1), and error-correction-prioritized sorting adds a further gain (69.9 SR, 64.9 SPL). GRPO alone yields better SPL/NE, while IL keeps OS high, so the two are complementary.
method: Model/memory: Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct in a StreamVLN-style multi-turn dialogue with long-term memory of n frames and short-term memory of m frames, with KV cache reuse; predicts chunks of 4 discrete actions (forward/left/right/stop)
Stage 1 multi-task training: co-train action prediction (793.4k samples from R2R, RxR, EnvDrop, ScaleVLN subset) and trajectory summarization (30.8k video-instruction pairs)

Stage 2 DAgger IL: collect trajectories with a heuristic mixed policy (oracle intervenes when deviation exceeds a threshold), replay all visited states to relabel with oracle action chunks instead of model-erroneous actions; 453.3k samples
Stage 3 on-policy GRPO: 8 rollouts per sample with rewards for format, exact match, position cosine similarity and normalized distance; token-level loss, KL β=0.1, clip ε=0.2

High-entropy trajectory sampling: record entropy of predicted action tokens during new DAgger collection (7.4k trajectories) and use only the top 20% highest-entropy samples (33.3k) for GRPO to avoid zero-advantage samples
CHORD joint loss: L=(1-μ)L_GRPO+μ L_IL with cosine decay of μ from 0.5 to 0.05 over the first 200 steps
Error-correction-prioritized sorting: rank IL trajectories by the proportion of oracle-corrected action tokens, most-corrected first (30.0k IL samples)

setting.training_data: Stage 1: 793.4k action samples (R2R, RxR, EnvDrop, ScaleVLN subset) + 30.8k trajectory-summarization pairs; Stage 2: 11.3k synthesized DAgger trajectories, 453.3k samples total; Stage 3: 7.4k new DAgger trajectories (33.3k GRPO samples, 30.0k IL samples)
setting.observation: monocular single RGB image (egocentric) with long/short-term frame memory
setting.action_space: discrete low-level actions (forward, left, right, stop), predicted in chunks of 4
setting.privileged: none at test time (oracle actions used only for DAgger training labels)

numbers.extra: single RGB; 3-stage training with ScaleVLN subset/EnvDrop data
numbers.evidence: Table 1 main comparison on VLN-CE R2R and RxR Val-Unseen; Table 2 row 7 CHORD-ec

numbers.method: Ablation row 6: Stage 3 CHORD (without error-correction sorting)

numbers_note: Real-world experiments are qualitative only, with no numbers.
results: JOP-VLN reaches 69.9 SR / 64.9 SPL / 3.64 NE on R2R-CE val-unseen with single RGB, beating CorrectNav (65.1 SR) among single-RGB methods and also panoramic NavFoM. OmniNav has 69.5 SR and 66.1 SPL. On RxR-CE it gets 68.0 SR / 59.3 SPL, below CorrectNav (69.3 SR) and OmniNav (73.6 SR).
limitations: On RxR-CE it does not beat CorrectNav or OmniNav, and its R2R SPL is below OmniNav
Real-world evaluation is only qualitative and needs 10-shot fine-tuning per environment, with failures on visually similar landmarks; 1.2s communication latency
Ablations cover only R2R; the entropy-sampling ratio (20%) and μ schedule are not ablated
